clue.text: Boris's hair? Prime minister cut the ends off

indicators.note: the closing letters of the prime minister's surname are chopped away, like trimming a fringe

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was British prime minister 1979-90

explanation.surface: A joke about a politician's famously messy mop and someone giving it a trim.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson, a recent UK prime minister, is known for untidy straw-coloured hair; removing ER from THATCHER leaves the roofing word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick untidy head of hair is jokingly likened to a straw roof covering, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Train from Bath East

parts.note: a bath is a tub
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A rail journey leaving the city of Bath heading eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath looks like the English city, but it is the thing you wash in.
explanation.definitionFit: London's underground railway and its trains are commonly called by this name.

clue.text: A c-competitor is coming

parts.note: the stammered c- shows the next word's opening letter said twice, so the synonym of competitor starts with a repeated letter
a competitor is a rival

explanation.surface: Someone stammering that a contestant is on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'c-competitor' tells you to stutter the synonym too: R-RIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is a coming, the act of reaching a place; both are nouns.

clue.text: Sort of bank on this route into university?

definitions.text: Sort of bank on this route into university?

parts.words: Sort of bank on this route into university?
parts.note: a ... bank is one type of bank, and in the UK ... is the late scheme matching unplaced students to spare university places

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about some kind of bank found along the way to college.
explanation.walkthrough: Two British senses: high-street clearing banks, and Clearing, the UCAS scheme after exam results for students without a university place.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a kind of bank that settles cheques and the UK late admissions route to degree courses.

clue.text: Badly-dressed seafood stuffed with cut of meat

indicators.note: the seafood word is filled with the cut of meat, like a stuffed fish

parts.note: fish is seafood
rump is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: A scruffy diner eating a fish filled with steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpish describes someone dowdy and dressed in dull, unfashionable clothes.

clue.text: Broadcast a serial, more to cheer us up

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A plea to a TV network to air more episodes of a series to lift viewers' spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as transmit, but it is the anagram signal on A SERIAL MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift spirits is to improve the collective mood of a group, the idiom meaning to make people feel more cheerful.

clue.text: Rockers' old rivals grab exercise bikes

indicators.note: the rivals hold the exercise abbreviation between them, as if grabbing it

parts.note: Mods and Rockers were rival British youth gangs of the 1960s
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Members of an old youth gang seize exercise cycles.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods, 1960s British scooter-riding youths, famously fought Rockers, who rode motorbikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopeds are small low-powered motorcycles, so they count as bikes.

clue.text: Orient's collapse is to come

indicators.note: a collapse brings the word down into a heap, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A prediction that Leyton Orient football club will fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a London football club; 'collapse' rearranges ORIENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awaiting us in the future is said to be lying ahead, the idiom meaning yet to happen.

clue.text: Like a lump fish? It's OK

parts.note: hunky can mean like a hunk, a thick lump
the dory is a sea fish, as in John Dory

explanation.surface: Asking whether a chunky fish is acceptable, then reassuring that it's fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is informal for fine or satisfactory, with everything going well.

clue.text: Like a tree? Dog may have

definitions.meaning: covered in bark, as a tree trunk is
a dog may have made its woofing sound

explanation.surface: A riddle linking trees and dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both clad in tree bark and having woofed, the past participle of the dog's call.

clue.text: Organ stop is sad — piano worse

indicators.note: the letters are made worse, knocked into a poorer order

explanation.surface: A complaint that an organ stop sounds gloomy and the piano is even worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapason is one of the main foundation stops on a pipe organ.

clue.text: No way will my relatives be crying here?

definitions.text: will my relatives be crying here?
definitions.meaning: mourners weep over a corpse, so relatives would cry over the speaker's lifeless form

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refusing and imagining their family weeping at their funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, literally the place mourners would weep beside a corpse.

clue.text: What makes cowards ill?

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, so a disease called yellow plus a word for illness would afflict cowards

explanation.surface: A question about what sickness strikes the timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow fever is a tropical viral disease; yellow is slang for cowardly, hence the joke.

clue.text: Hold son?

parts.note: taking half of the admiral's name Nelson leaves its last three letters, which are the clue's word

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether to hold a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: half of NELSON is SON, the clue's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A half nelson is a wrestling hold, an arm lock applied from behind.

clue.text: Batsman's aggressive strategy found by accident?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, striking the ball and setting off at once for a quick single
a road collision where the driver flees the scene

explanation.surface: A cricketer's attacking approach turned up by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found by accident' reads as discovered by luck; really 'accident' names a collision where the driver escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both an attacking cricket or baseball tactic and a collision whose driver flees.

clue.text: Ban means nothing to surgeon

indicators.note: the zero is added to the surgeon word, joined after it

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A prohibition means nothing to a defiant surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a formal prohibition or the power to block a proposal.

clue.text: His sounds a possible career?

parts.note: someone whose sounds are a career is a performer of music; 'His sounds' can also be read as MUSIC plus IAN, a man's name

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some man's noises could become a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A player or composer makes a career out of the sounds they produce.

clue.text: Dog, or part of it

definitions.meaning: to dog is to follow closely, shadow
a section of a dog, the wagging end

explanation.surface: A dog, or just one bit of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to follow someone secretly, and the appendage at a dog's rear.

clue.text: At home more healthy to have respirator

parts.note: in means at home
haler is the comparative of hale, healthy

explanation.surface: Staying indoors and being fitter lets someone use breathing equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is a device for breathing medicine into the lungs, a kind of respirator.

clue.text: Is that all you can say?

definitions.text: Is that all you can say?

parts.words: Is that all you can say?
parts.note: read literally, the question asks for the full stock of words one can speak

explanation.surface: An exasperated retort to a feeble reply.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lexicon is literally everything one is able to say, the whole stock of known words.

clue.text: Agony, using a dreadful hotel

indicators.note: a dreadful version of the words is a mangled one, so they are rearranged

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pain caused by staying in an awful hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering, a close synonym of torment.

clue.text: Poor chap's attempt to be sick is heard

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by how the word sounds rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: to retch is to try to vomit

explanation.surface: An unfortunate man audibly gagging.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is an unfortunate, pitiable person.

clue.text: Lacking rigid opinions, I am not offended

definitions.meaning: taken literally: having no firm views or emotions
said to show you bear no grudge

explanation.surface: Someone open-minded telling another person they took no offence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase reassures that no resentment is held, and literally means without firm sentiments.

clue.text: Clothes one changes in the car

definitions.meaning: the driver shifts this to alter speed

explanation.surface: Someone getting changed into different clothes inside a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both informal clothing and the toothed mechanism a driver selects.

clue.text: Corresponding with one of the family

definitions.meaning: proportionate or comparative, considered in relation to something

explanation.surface: Writing letters to a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corresponding with' suggests exchanging letters; 'with' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means comparative or proportional, and also a kinsman or member of one's family.

clue.text: Show pleasure about one turn of phrase

indicators.note: the smile goes round the numeral, surrounding it

parts.note: to smile is to show pleasure
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone delighted by a clever expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech comparing things with like or as.

clue.text: In one quarter, no respite at first given to our sailors

indicators.note: the sailors are attached to the end of what precedes
only the opening letter of respite is wanted

parts.note: our sailors are the RN, the Royal Navy, with the article included

explanation.surface: Sailors stationed somewhere get no rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our sailors' is THE RN: the Royal Navy is the British navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Northern means situated in the north, one of the four compass quarters.

clue.text: Hold firm in an endlessly boring task

indicators.note: the task word loses its last letter, so it has no end

parts.note: a chore is a boring task

explanation.surface: Staying resolute through a tedious, never-ending job.
explanation.definitionFit: To anchor is to fix firmly in place, like a ship held by its heavy hook.
